question: Can the Stage49 H-parameter hardness survive strictly binary positive-edge trees while retaining the supplied cap+1 explanation promise?

main_result.answer: Yes according to the complete construction and soundness proof in stage50_binary_theory.json; finite validation found no contradiction.
main_result.model: Known reduced unrooted tree; every internal original vertex has degree exactly 3; positive rational original edge lengths; distances observed only at a subset of original leaves; prescribed mean pendant 1; normalized positive sources strictly inside distinct original edges.
main_result.theorem: Exact minimum-source decision is W[1]-hard parameterized by source budget H, even when a strict explanation with at most H+1 sources is supplied as part of the input.
main_result.gap: The constructed YES instances have strict minimum H and NO instances have strict minimum H+1. NO excludes even closed point sources, including vertices and repeated edges.
main_result.source_parameter: K positive integer SUM lists map to H=K+1; t-Multicolored Clique maps to H=t+binomial(t,2)+1 or a constant-budget NO instance.
main_result.new_ingredient: A single forced calibration source absorbs positive binary-core deformation through an exact rational linear solve. Unit hidden-edge depth and the fixed pendant enforce a mass interval too narrow to hide an incorrect integer sum.
main_result.exact_forward_equation: (diag(1/(1+a_i))+Bcore)p=c*1+h/2, with c=1/[2(K+target)] and positive semidefinite shared-path Bcore.
main_result.reverse_integer_bound: Any cap-H competitor forces one positive-depth hidden source per active arm and one calibration source; its selected integer sum S obeys |S-target|<17/240<1.
main_result.supplied_witness: Greedy interpolation of group minima/maxima uses at most one split group; the same exact solve then produces at most H+1 strict sources without solving SUM.
main_result.complexity: Input tree, observations and supplied witness have polynomial binary encoding length; exact rational elimination has polynomial bit complexity.
main_result.integer_corollary: Scaling every edge by the LCM L of edge and (d-1) denominators and setting d_new=1+L*(d_old-1) preserves pendant 1 and all source explanations bidirectionally. This gives positive integer lengths and observations, but loses the edge<=1 restriction and does not imply strong hardness.
main_result.interpretation: Under FPT!=W[1], the arbitrary-missing-leaf prescribed-pendant problem does not admit an H-only FPT algorithm even on strictly binary trees. This is consistent with the Stage48 2^{O(H+J)} upper bound.

constructive_development.scope: Exact constructive witnesses and binary topology; does not certify NO instances

frozen_confirmation.method: Generic original-edge support enumeration with exact rational nonnegative endpoint feasibility; range screening reads only original distances, never reduction metadata. Closed NO plus strict cap+1 witness certifies strict minimum cap+1; closed minimum cap plus independent strict cap witness certifies strict minimum cap.
frozen_confirmation.derived_inputs: 14 inputs = 12 new base inputs + 2 deterministic integer rescalings; not 14 independent base cases.

full_composition.scope: Construction replay does not independently decide the large NO PDD instances; their NO statement follows from the audited reduction proof and inherited incidence encoding
full_composition.extra_boundary_fact: Every nonempty valid incidence encoding already has target inside the continuous group-sum interval; the defensive outside-interval branch is unreachable for that source encoding. Empty-pair graph NO maps to fixed SUM NO [[1,3],[1,3]],target3.

Independent review of both exact closed oracles found range screening, duplicate endpoint merging and source reconstruction complete under the original-edge cap.
Additional boundary review checked the supplied-witness promise for circular reasoning, constant NO mapping, rational bit complexity and integer rescaling.
All reviews are internal AI-assisted checks; no external human review is claimed.

prior_work_boundary.stage16_comparison: Earlier binary NP-hardness used source budget depending on input item count N and did not imply H-only W[1]-hardness or the supplied H+1 gap.

Finite checks supplement but do not establish the asymptotic proof or novelty.
